samples.summary: `Doc.batch` only re-syncs its cache on the throw path; a *successful* batch whose body writes straight through `this.store.*` leaves `_document` stale
samples.evidence: `batch(fn)` calls `this.store.batch(fn)` and refreshes only inside `catch`. The doc comment promises it keeps "this cache consistent with what actually landed", but nothing refreshes after a successful commit. The single current caller, `withNamedStyleChange` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1087), writes via `docStore.setDocStyles` / `updateStyleDefinition` / `resetStyle` / `resetAllStyles` — store-level calls that never touch `Doc._document` — and is only saved because `doc.dropStaleStyleOffAll()` (document.ts:543) happens to begin with `this.refresh()`. Any future body that omits a `Doc`-level write, or a change that makes `dropStaleStyleOffAll` return early before its leading refresh, silently leaves `_document` describing the pre-batch document while the store holds the post-batch one, and `getBlock`/layout/paint all answer from it. A `finally { this.refresh(); }` (or refresh on both paths) would make the contract match the comment.

samples.summary: On a throw inside `withNamedStyleChange`, layout/paint are never invalidated even though `MemDocStore` keeps the partial writes
samples.evidence: `invalidateLayout(); render(); notifyStyleApplied();` sit after `doc.batch(...)`, so an exception escaping the batch skips all three. For `YorkieDocStore` that is fine (the update rolls back). For `MemDocStore` the partial writes stand — `MemDocStore.batch` explicitly documents "On a throw the partial writes stand (this store does not roll back)" (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:206-208) — and the new `Doc.batch` catch then refreshes `_document` to that partial state. The model now differs from the cached layout/painted output, so the editor renders stale metrics/styles for the affected blocks until some unrelated edit forces a relayout. Re-syncing the cache without re-invalidating layout makes the two caches disagree.

samples.summary: `Doc.batch`'s catch can replace the original error with a refresh error, losing the root cause and leaving the cache stale
samples.evidence: ```catch (err) { this.refresh(); throw err; }``` — `refresh()` calls `store.getDocument()`, which for `YorkieDocStore` re-reads the Yorkie root right after `doc.update` discarded its contaminated clone (yorkie-doc-store.ts:628-652 → `readRoot()` → `this.doc.getRoot()`). If that read throws (tree missing/rebuild failure), the `throw err` line is never reached: the caller sees a secondary error instead of the real failure, and `_document` is left holding the uncommitted state this wrapper exists to discard. Wrapping the refresh in its own try/catch would keep the original error primary.

samples.summary: Rolled-back batch leaves `localCursorAnchor`/`localSelectionAnchor`/`pendingCursorPos` anchored to a discarded Yorkie clone
samples.evidence: `batch()`'s `finally` resets only `dirty`/`cachedDoc` when the update did not commit. Anchors written during the batch (e.g. via `setCursorForHistory` → `anchorDocPosition`, which now reads the *ambient* root at line 968 thanks to `readRoot()`) were computed against the clone Yorkie throws away, so after a rollback they reference tree positions that never existed in the committed CRDT. `resolveAnchoredDocPosition` (line 1113) swallows the resulting failure and falls back, so the cost is a silently wrong caret/selection restore rather than a crash — but the store-side state is not rolled back alongside the cache the way `Doc.batch` now rolls back its own.

finding.summary: Several read paths still call `this.doc.getRoot()` while the batch's `doc.update` is open; correctness of the whole batch rests on an unverified SDK assumption and no test exercises it
finding.evidence: `withUpdate` routes writes to the ambient root, but reads do not: `getDocument()` falls through to `this.doc.getRoot()` whenever `dirty` is true (line 611-635), and `readDocStyles()` (645), `getPageSetup()` (685), `setHeader`/`setFooter` (710/749) and `anchorDocPosition()` (953) call it unconditionally. Inside a top-level `batch()` these all execute while the batch's single `doc.update` is still open — e.g. `writeStylesAndRematerialize` calls `this.getDocument()` (line 2787) from inside the batch, and `updateCursorPos` still runs `anchorDocPosition` mid-batch (line 3147-3150) mixing a raw `getRoot()` tree read with cache-derived block paths. The only justification is the prose at line 2835-2838 ("Reads … are safe inside an open update"); if `getRoot()` instead returns pre-update state (or the SDK refuses it), tree indices and cached document would disagree, producing wrong tree paths / caret anchors. Every new batch test seeds the cache with `setDocument()` first, so the `dirty === true` entry into a batch (the normal state right after a remote change) is never exercised.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is not present. All read paths named in the finding route through the `readRoot()` seam at yorkie-doc-store.ts:624-626 (`return this.activeRoot ?? this.doc.getRoot();`), which returns the batch's ambient root while a top-level `batch()` is open: getDocument() :632, readDocStyles() :662, getPageSetup() :702, setHeader() :727, setFooter() :766, anchorDocPosition() :970. A grep for `doc.getRoot()` in this file yields exactly one live call site, :625 inside readRoot() itself; the other two hits (:616, :2855) are comment text. The specific mid-batch cases cited are internally consistent rather than mixed: writeStylesAndRematerialize (:2803-2833) reads via this.getDocument() (:2804) which goes through readRoot(), and anchorDocPosition takes both its tree (:970) and its currentDoc (:974) from the same ambient root. The prose quoted as the sole justification ("Reads … are safe inside an open update") does not exist; the actual comment at :615-622 states that depending on getRoot() observing in-progress writes would rest on an SDK internal and that reading the ambient root "removes the assumption", and :2852-2855 points at readRoot as the read-side rule. Lines 2835-2838 are cache-update statements, not a justification. The remaining test-coverage point is out of the correctness lane and rests on the same refuted premise.
